text:
nora: Quick sync on reducing dashboard query CPU: spike analysis suggests we fetch lots of columns and then apply RBAC filters late in the plan. We should evaluate projection / auth pushdown in planner instead of ad-hoc app-side hacks.

devon: Agree. Long-term solution is integrating auth as a logical predicate so optimizer can reorder and avoid large joins. But we need an incremental path.

kai: Sketch: introduce an AuthPredicate interface in planner that can be treated like any other predicate. Initially it would be lowered to either 1) an index lookup (permission index service) or 2) an auth-join fallback.

priya: Permission index service? Explain.

kai: Small service that, given tenant + principal + resource-type + predicate, returns allowed resource ids or a bitmap. Implemented as fast cache backed by DB. Planner can replace auth join with IN(allowed_ids) or a semi-join against bitmap.

devon: This avoids pushing full auth logic into the executor. Planner emits a plan that asks the permission-index via a prefetch operator. That's invasive but incremental: start with prefetch operator as optional.

nora: Example plan snippet:
```
Filter(predicate: updated_at > now()-7d AND auth_pred(dashboard))
 |- Sort(last_used DESC)
    |- Scan(dashboards)
```
becomes
```
PrefetchPerms(principal, tenant, resource_type=dashboard) -> allowed_ids
Filter(updated_at > now()-7d AND id IN allowed_ids)
 |- Sort(...)
    |- Scan(dashboards)
```

priya: Nice. That prefetch can run once per query and reduces row-level auth checks. But we must handle large allowed_ids sets (admins). How to avoid giant IN lists?

kai: Two options: return a compressed bitmap or a predicate token that indicates "covers all within tenant". If bitmap size > threshold, planner chooses fallback auth-join or keeps original plan. We can also pass hints: admin=true => short-circuit.

devon: API for permission-index should support: 1) exact id set (limited size), 2) bitmap compressed, 3) coverage hint (full-tenant or namespace). Keep it simple initially: id set + coverage flag.

nora: Rollout strategy: Phase 0: add AuthPredicate abstraction + no-op planner path. Phase 1: add PrefetchPerms operator and permission-index prototype in dev env (internal only). Phase 2: enable for owner/admin dashboard routes for low-risk tenants. Phase 3: broader rollout and optimize bitmap path.

priya: Telemetry we need: planner_fastpath_enabled, prefetch_latency, allowed_ids_count, plan_change_rate, cpu_per_query. Also correctness checks: random sample queries do full auth-join compare to prefetch results.

kai: Security: permission-index must verify caller identity (service token), encrypt traffic, and honour revocations. We'll include a rev_version field so we can invalidate caches.

devon: Ops concerns: prefetch operator adds an external call during planning/execution. We should make it asynchronous where executor can block on prefetch result but with a bounded timeout. If prefetch fails, fallback to current auth-join.

nora: Implementation owners: kai - add AuthPredicate & PrefetchPerms operator + planner tests. priya - permission-index proto and auth rules. devon - telemetry + perf harness to simulate tenant workloads.

ops-bot: Incident reminder: permission-index service must be ready for autoscaling triggers. See infra runbook.

priya: Can we get a quick spike to measure allowed_ids size distribution for top 50 tenants? If most sets are small it's a win.

nora: I'll run the sampling job this afternoon and post numbers. Acceptance criteria for first canary: median CPU/query down 30% and no auth-mismatch in 1000 sampled queries.

devon: Sounds good. Keep RFC note: long-term unify auth semantics into logical model so optimizer can cost auth predicates. This prefetch path is an engineering compromise.

nora: OK action items listed. We'll reconvene after the sampling job. :white_check_mark:
